questions.q: Which pair of compounds can be distinguished by Fehling's solution?
questions.explain: Only ethanal, an aliphatic aldehyde, gives red Cu₂O; benzaldehyde, an aromatic aldehyde, leaves the solution blue. Benzaldehyde and propanone are both negative, while glucose/fructose and ethanal/propanal are both positive.

questions.q: The reddish-brown precipitate formed in a positive Fehling's test is:
questions.explain: The aldehyde reduces Cu²⁺ to Cu⁺, which separates as copper(I) oxide: RCHO + 2Cu²⁺ + 5OH⁻ → RCOO⁻ + Cu₂O + 3H₂O. Copper metal (a mirror) is not formed; that is the silver result of Tollens' test.

questions.q: The role of sodium potassium tartrate (Rochelle salt) in Fehling's solution B is to:
options: Oxidise the aldehyde to an acid
Complex Cu²⁺ so that Cu(OH)₂ does not precipitate in the alkali
questions.explain: Tartrate is a ligand that holds Cu²⁺ in solution as a deep blue bis(tartrato)cuprate(II) complex in strongly basic medium. Cu²⁺ itself is the oxidant, and the reagent is alkaline (NaOH), not acidic.

questions.q: In exam answers, which compound is counted as giving a red precipitate when heated with Fehling's solution?
questions.explain: A gem-dichloride R–CHCl₂ hydrolyses in the hot alkaline reagent to the aldehyde RCHO, which then reduces Cu²⁺. Benzaldehyde, propanone and acetic acid all leave the solution blue; formic acid is the only simple acid that reacts.
